title: Monte Verde archaeological site
note: Los Lagos, Chile (UNESCO Tentative List 1873, coords 41°30'17" S, 73°12'16" W). MV-II ~14,500 cal BP (Dillehay et al. 2015, PMC4651426) versus mid-Holocene 8,200–4,200 BP (Surovell et al. 2026, Science doi:10.1126/science.adw9217) and the May 2026 eLetter rebuttals. Strongly contested; needs perspectives. Place kind, importance likely 3 or more, so a model is needed (structure footprint from Dillehay's excavation reports).

title: White Sands human footprints (Locality 2)
note: Bennett et al. 2021 (Bournemouth author manuscript), Pigati et al. 2022 reply and 2023 pollen/OSL study, Oviatt et al. 2022 Quaternary Research critique; USGS data releases 10.5066/P9ABZEM9 and 10.5066/P9E36U4B; NPS footprint pages (sloth-stalking trackway, woman-and-child trackway of 2018).

title: Anzick-1 (Clovis infant burial, Montana)
note: Named archaeological individual: site 24PA506, Park County; 10,705 ± 35 14C BP (12,707–12,556 cal BP); red ochre, ~100 stone and 15 osseous Clovis tools; genome (Rasmussen et al. 2014, PMC4878442); tribal consultation and requested reburial. Handle respectfully; check reburial outcome in later sources.

title: Clovis complex
note: 13,050–12,750 cal BP from 32 dates at 10 sites (Waters et al. 2020, PMC7577710); short versus long chronologies; the Clovis-first model and its abandonment; Clovis end and proboscidean extinction.

title: Fishtail (Fell) projectile point complex of South America
note: Established in the southern cone by ~12,900 cal BP (Waters et al. 2020); continent-wide distribution (Potter et al. 2018). South America before 1492 is under-recorded; find Patagonian site literature (Fell's Cave, Pali Aike).

title: Beringian standstill
note: Tamm et al. 2007 (PMC1952074) founder mtDNA lineages; Upward Sun River genome and Ancient Beringians (Moreno-Mayar et al. 2018, Nature; reviewed by Potter et al. 2018, PMC6082647); location of isolation contested (Beringia versus anywhere from Cis-Baikal to Hokkaido). Region: Beringia spans Russia and Alaska.

title: Huaca Prieta early coastal occupation, Peru
note: Named by Potter et al. 2018 with Monte Verde as an early near-coastal South American site; check Dillehay et al. (Science Advances 2017) for dates and open access.
